argv:
You generate synthetic meeting transcripts with gold annotations for LiveMinutes, a research dataset modeled on the AMI Meeting Corpus scenario meetings.

In AMI scenario meetings, a team of four plays a design team in a fictional company. The roles are Project Manager (PM), Marketing Expert (ME), User Interface designer (UI) and Industrial Designer (ID). A series has four meetings: (a) kickoff, (b) functional design, (c) conceptual design, (d) detailed design. Later meetings refer back to earlier ones.

Write natural spoken conversation the way AMI transcripts read: short turns, fillers ("um", "uh", "yeah"), backchannels ("mm-hmm", "okay"), interruptions, people building on each other, and some disfluency. Do not write a screenplay. Do not narrate. No stage directions.

Each segment is one dialogue-act-like unit: one speaker, usually one clause or short sentence, sometimes just a backchannel. Give each segment an AMI dialogue-act type from this set:
  bck backchannel, stl stall, fra fragment, inf inform, sug suggest, ass assess,
  el.inf elicit-inform, el.sug elicit-offer-or-suggestion, el.ass elicit-assessment,
  el.und elicit-comment-understanding, off offer, und comment-about-understanding,
  be.pos be-positive, be.neg be-negative, oth other

Absent participants NEVER speak. Speaker labels are ground truth: use only the labels you are given.

The gold annotations must be exactly true of the transcript you write. Refer to segments by their "n" number. Every number you cite must exist.

Output a single JSON object and nothing else: no prose, no markdown fences.

request.user:
Write meeting SY0301d: meeting "d" (detailed design) of series SY0301.

PROJECT
The team is designing a library self-checkout kiosk.

PARTICIPANTS (label, role, status for this meeting)
A  User Interface designer (UI)  Tomas  present
B  Project Manager (PM)  Helen  present
C  Marketing Expert (ME)  Rafael  present
D  Industrial Designer (ID)  Ingrid  present

EARLIER MEETINGS IN THIS SERIES
Stay consistent with them. Refer back to them, follow up on their open action items, and keep the same product and team.

[SY0301a, kickoff]
  abstract: The project manager opened the kickoff meeting and the team introduced themselves. She presented the brief: a self-checkout kiosk for the Northfield library consortium's twelve branches, about forty units, with a production cost under 2,500 euros per unit. The team agreed that the kiosk will handle checkout only, because returns are already covered by the book drops and would need extra hardware. The marketing expert said the users range from children to older people, so the user interface designer wants large text, few steps (around three screens) and a screen height that works for wheelchair users. The industrial designer suggested a tiltable screen. The industrial designer declared that the kiosk would use RFID only. The marketing expert and the user interface designer raised concerns about untagged collections and cost, and the project manager deferred the question without a decision. The project manager first asked the marketing expert to arrange a branch site visit. She cancelled this once she remembered the client had supplied a staff and borrower survey, and asked him to analyse the survey instead.
  decisions: The kiosk will support checkout only. Returns are excluded.
  actions: The industrial designer will research the scanner options and other components and what they cost. The user interface designer will work on the screen flow and look at accessibility guidelines. The marketing expert will go through the client's survey, pull out the main user requirements and present them at the next meeting. He will also look for anything on RFID and on receipt preferences. The project manager will circulate the brief, the survey file and the minutes.
  problems: Whether the kiosk should read RFID tags, barcodes or both is unresolved. The team does not know which branches have RFID-tagged collections. It is unclear whether an RFID reader fits within the 2,500 euro per-unit budget, which the team considers tight. Whether receipts should be printed or emailed is open, pending the survey results.
  action item SY0301a.ai1: Research scanner options and other components and their costs (owner D, active)
  action item SY0301a.ai2: Work on the interface screen flow and look at accessibility guidelines (owner A, active)
  action item SY0301a.ai3: Contact branch staff and arrange a site visit to the main town-centre library to observe current checkout (owner C, dropped)
  action item SY0301a.ai4: Go through the client's staff and borrower survey and bring the main user requirements to the next meeting, including anything on RFID and receipts (owner C, active)
  action item SY0301a.ai5: Circulate the project brief, the survey file and the minutes (owner B, active)
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The industrial designer declared the kiosk would use RFID only. Nobody agreed, and the project manager deferred the question.
  fact (action_item_removed): The project manager cancelled the site visit task because the client's survey already covers user needs.
  fact (plan_change): The marketing expert's task changed from arranging a site visit to analysing the existing survey.

[SY0301b, functional design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the functional design meeting, noted that the user interface designer was absent through illness, and confirmed she had circulated the brief, survey file and minutes from the kickoff. The marketing expert presented the survey results. Borrowers mainly want speed, independence from staff and readable screens. About sixty percent prefer emailed receipts, but most respondents over sixty-five want a printed slip. Staff comments show RFID tagging is patchy across branches, and the survey has no clear list of tagged branches. The industrial designer presented component costs, about 2,100 euros per unit with everything included. She withdrew her earlier RFID-only position, and the team agreed the kiosk will read both RFID tags and barcodes. The team also agreed that users choose email, print or both on the final screen. The marketing expert's suggestion of fine payment at the kiosk was set aside as out of scope. The project manager assigned the absent user interface designer the scanning and receipt screen flow and the wheelchair height and tilt work.
  decisions: The kiosk will read both RFID tags and barcodes. Receipts will be offered by email, print or both, chosen on the final screen, and a thermal printer will be included.
  actions: The user interface designer, who was absent, was given a task by the project manager. He will work out the screen flow for the scanning screen and the receipt choice so that it supports both RFID and barcode within three screens. He will also define the screen height and tilt range for wheelchair users. The marketing expert will contact the consortium for a list of which branches have RFID-tagged collections. The industrial designer will prepare a detailed cost breakdown with both scanners and the printer, including a closer look at the casing, for the conceptual design meeting. The project manager will email the user interface designer the minutes and his task.
  problems: It is still unknown which branches have fully RFID-tagged collections. The estimated cost of about 2,100 euros per unit leaves little margin under the 2,500 euro limit, and the casing cost is uncertain.
  action item SY0301b.ai1: Work out the screen flow for the scanning screen and receipt choice so it supports both RFID and barcode within three screens, and define the screen height and tilt range for wheelchair users (owner A, active)
  action item SY0301b.ai2: Price up an RFID-only version of the kiosk for comparison (owner D, dropped)
  action item SY0301b.ai3: Contact the consortium to get a list of which branches have RFID-tagged collections (owner C, active)
  action item SY0301b.ai4: Prepare a detailed cost breakdown with both scanners and the printer, including the casing, for the conceptual design meeting (owner D, active)
  action item SY0301b.ai5: Email the absent user interface designer the minutes and his task (owner B, active)
  fact (absence): The user interface designer (Tomas, A) was absent from this meeting because he was off sick.
  fact (action_item_removed): The project manager cancelled the RFID-only costing. The only difference was the 120 euro barcode scanner, and the team then decided to include both scanners.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert suggested the kiosk could take fine payments. The project manager set it aside as beyond the brief.
  fact (plan_change): The industrial designer dropped her earlier RFID-only position because of patchy tagging, and supported using both RFID and barcode.

[SY0301c, conceptual design]
  abstract: The project manager opened the conceptual design meeting and noted that the user interface designer was absent again, this time on a training course. She confirmed she had emailed him the minutes and his task from the functional design meeting, and said he had not yet sent his screen flow. The marketing expert reported the consortium's RFID list: seven of the twelve branches are fully tagged, three are partly tagged and two have no RFID. This confirmed the earlier decision to read both RFID tags and barcodes. He added that all library cards carry a barcode, so no separate card reader is needed. The industrial designer presented a full cost breakdown of 1,940 euros per unit before the casing. A brushed steel casing would bring the total to about 2,360 euros, and a moulded plastic casing to about 2,200 euros. She dropped her preference for steel, and the team chose moulded plastic and a freestanding pedestal. The marketing expert's statement that the idle screen would show library event adverts was not taken up, and the meeting moved on. The team provisionally favoured the consortium's green, pending the consortium's style guide. The project manager gave the absent user interface designer an extra task: mock-ups of the three screens. She also asked him to send his height and tilt range to the industrial designer.
  decisions: Library cards will be scanned with the barcode scanner, so there will be no separate card reader. The kiosk will have a moulded plastic casing instead of brushed steel, giving an estimated cost of about 2,200 euros per unit. The kiosk will be a freestanding pedestal unit.
  actions: The user interface designer, who was absent, will continue the screen flow for scanning and the receipt choice and the wheelchair height and tilt range, as assigned at the functional design meeting. The user interface designer, who was absent, was assigned by the project manager to produce mock-ups of the three screens on the 21-inch screen in the consortium green for the detailed design meeting. The user interface designer will send his height and tilt range to the industrial designer as soon as he has it, so that she can finalise the pedestal. The project manager will email the user interface designer about his new tasks. The marketing expert will ask the consortium whether it has a branding style guide. The industrial designer will get a proper quote for the plastic casing mould. The industrial designer will build a rough foam model of the pedestal for the detailed design meeting.
  problems: The colour is only provisionally the consortium green and depends on the consortium's style guide. The plastic casing cost of 260 euros is a catalogue figure and still needs a real quote. The pedestal and screen height cannot be finalised until the user interface designer supplies his height and tilt range, and his screen flow has not yet been delivered. Three branches are only partly RFID-tagged. The consortium expects tagging to be completed in about a year but would not commit to this.
  action item SY0301c.ai1: Work out the screen flow for scanning and the receipt choice, and define the wheelchair height and tilt range (carried over from SY0301b) (owner A, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai2: Produce mock-ups of the three screens on the 21-inch screen in the consortium green for the detailed design meeting (owner A, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai3: Send the height and tilt range to the industrial designer as soon as it is available, so she can finalise the pedestal (owner A, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai4: Email the absent user interface designer his new tasks (the mock-ups and the height and tilt range for the industrial designer) (owner B, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai5: Ask the consortium whether it has branding rules or a style guide (owner C, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai6: Get a proper quote for the moulded plastic casing mould (owner D, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai7: Make a rough foam model of the pedestal for the detailed design meeting (owner D, active)
  action item SY0301c.ai8: Ask the branches how much floor space they have for the kiosk (owner C, dropped)
  fact (absence): The user interface designer (Tomas, A) was absent from the conceptual design meeting because he was on a training course all week.
  fact (plan_change): The industrial designer originally wanted a steel casing, but switched to plastic because of the budget margin.
  fact (unagreed_proposal): The marketing expert stated as if it were decided that the idle screen would show adverts for library events. Nobody agreed, and the project manager moved on to colours without settling it.
  fact (action_item_removed): The marketing expert's offer to ask the branches about floor space was dropped by the project manager, because the pedestal is only about 60 by 60 cm.

EDGE CASES THIS MEETING MUST CONTAIN
Weave each one naturally into the project discussion. Each must be clearly present, and each must be tagged with the segments where it happens.
- F3_ACTION_REMOVED [F3]: An action item is created and later in the same meeting explicitly removed or cancelled. The action item has status dropped. Record an F3 fact of type action_item_removed linked to it.
  Required gold labels: action_items, qa_facts, edge_cases.
- F3_UNAGREED_DECISION [F3]: Someone raises a proposal as if it were a decision, but no one agrees to it and the meeting moves on without settling it. Record an F3 fact of type unagreed_proposal with agreed false. It must not appear in summary.decisions.
  Required gold labels: summary, qa_facts, edge_cases.

LENGTH
Between 90 and 140 segments.

GOLD LABELS
- summary: AMI-style abstractive summary in third person, using role names ("The project manager ..."). Sections: abstract (3-6 sentences), actions, decisions, problems (open issues). It reflects the meeting's FINAL state: corrected values, final plans, and no jokes or tangents reported as content.
- action_items: every task arising in the meeting. owner is the speaker label of the FINAL owner, and may be an absent participant. owner is null ONLY for a task nobody takes, with owner_unclear true. status is the final status: active, reassigned (owner changed; previous_owners lists earlier owners) or dropped. history lists the events in order. evidence_segments lists the supporting segments.
- qa_facts: atomic facts someone could later ask about ("Who was asked to ...?", "Did the team agree on ...?"). Include every decision (agreed true), every proposal nobody agreed to (type unagreed_proposal, agreed false), action items, removed action items, absences, and plan changes. Because this meeting follows earlier ones, include at least one fact of type reference_to_prior_meeting, with refers_to_meeting set, at a point where someone refers back to an earlier meeting. Do NOT write questions.
- edge_cases: one entry per edge case above, with its scenario_id and the segment numbers that contain it.

OUTPUT JSON SHAPE
{
  "segments": [{"n": 1, "speaker": "A", "da_type": "inf", "text": "..."}],
  "summary": {"abstract": ["..."], "actions": ["..."], "decisions": ["..."], "problems": ["..."]},
  "action_items": [{"n": 1, "description": "...", "owner": "C", "owner_unclear": false, "status": "active", "previous_owners": [], "history": [{"segment": 12, "event": "assigned", "by": "A", "owner": "C"}], "evidence_segments": [12, 13]}],
  "qa_facts": [{"type": "decision", "fact": "...", "agreed": true, "related_action_item": null, "refers_to_meeting": null, "evidence_segments": [40]}],
  "edge_cases": [{"scenario_id": "...", "segments": [20, 21, 22], "note": "one line on how it appears"}]
}
history events: proposed, offered, assigned, accepted, reassigned, dropped, restated. qa_facts types: decision, unagreed_proposal, action_item, action_item_removed, absence, plan_change, reference_to_prior_meeting, other. related_action_item is an action item's "n" or null. refers_to_meeting is an earlier meeting ID of this series or null.
